$schema_comment: RaceLab universal RC setup ONTOLOGY — the backbone the deterministic race engineer reasons over. Three lists: parameters (canonical adjustable settings), symptoms (pilot complaints), option_classes (model-gated availability). param_id convention is aligned with the engine's existing `setting:` ids (front_shock_oil, rear_sway_bar, rear_anti_squat, ride_height_rake, shock_pistons, caster, etc.). applies_to values: 'all', 'offroad', 'onroad', plus scale/discipline tags (1-8-offroad, 1-10-2wd, 1-10-4wd, touring, pan, f1, truggy, short-course, monster-truck, crawler, rally, large-scale, gt). option_part=true means the adjustment is NOT present on every model and the engineer MUST gate advice on the exact chassis (see option_classes). Grounded in established RC setup engineering (HUDY Off-Road Set-Up Book, JQRacing THE Guide, XRAY/TLR/AE/Kyosho factory setup sheets, So Dialed conventions).

parameters.label: Front camber
parameters.what_it_does: Tilt of the front wheels from vertical (negative = tops leaning in). More negative camber loads the outer tyre's contact patch when the chassis rolls in a corner, increasing peak front grip but reducing straight-line patch and tyre life.

parameters.label: Rear camber
parameters.what_it_does: Tilt of the rear wheels from vertical. More negative rear camber increases rear cornering grip under roll at the cost of forward bite on corner exit and straight-line traction.

parameters.label: Front toe
parameters.what_it_does: Steer angle of the front wheels at rest (toe-out = leading edges apart, toe-in = together). Toe-out sharpens corner-entry steering and turn-in response; toe-in calms it and adds straight-line and entry stability.

parameters.label: Rear toe
parameters.what_it_does: Built-in toe-in at the rear axle. More rear toe-in adds rear stability and straight-line tracking and reduces on-power oversteer, but slows rotation and scrubs some top speed.

parameters.label: Front caster
parameters.what_it_does: Rearward tilt of the front kingpin/steering axis. More caster adds on-power steering and high-speed straight-line stability and smooths bump steering, but reduces off-power/initial turn-in and low-speed steering.

parameters.label: Caster (alias of front_caster)
parameters.what_it_does: Engine-canonical alias for front caster used by existing rules. Rearward steering-axis tilt; more = more on-power and high-speed steering, less initial bite.

parameters.label: Front anti-dive
parameters.what_it_does: Angle of the front suspension pivots that resists nose-dive under braking/deceleration. More anti-dive keeps the front higher on entry, calming initial steering and reducing diving into bumps; less frees up entry steering.

parameters.label: Rear anti-squat
parameters.what_it_does: Angle of the rear suspension pivots that resists the rear squatting under acceleration. More anti-squat plants the rear and adds forward bite/wheelstand on power but can unsettle the car over rough on-power sections; less smooths bumpy acceleration.

parameters.label: Front roll center
parameters.what_it_does: Height of the front geometric roll axis, set by inner/outer camber-link positions. A higher front roll center reduces front body roll for quicker, more aggressive steering response; lower rolls more for smoother, higher peak grip.

parameters.label: Rear roll center
parameters.what_it_does: Height of the rear geometric roll axis, set by camber-link positions. Higher rear roll center reduces rear roll for more aggressive, less progressive rear grip; lower adds roll for smoother, more forgiving rear traction.

parameters.label: Ackermann
parameters.what_it_does: How much more the inner front wheel steers than the outer (steering-block/bellcrank geometry). More Ackermann adds aggressive initial/low-speed steering; less makes steering smoother and more linear through the corner.

parameters.label: Wheelbase
parameters.what_it_does: Front-to-rear axle distance, set by rear-hub shims or chassis position. Longer wheelbase adds high-speed and jumping stability and smooths the car; shorter increases agility and rotation.

parameters.label: Front track width
parameters.what_it_does: Outer width of the front axle, set by wheel/hub shims. Wider front reduces front roll for more stability and less steering; narrower increases roll and steering response.

parameters.label: Rear track width
parameters.what_it_does: Outer width of the rear axle, set by wheel/hub shims. Wider rear reduces rear roll and adds rear stability/traction-roll resistance; narrower increases rear roll and rotation.

parameters.label: Kick-up angle
parameters.what_it_does: Upward angle of the front arms/chassis at the front pivot. More kick-up helps the front climb over and absorb bumps and resists nose-diving in ruts, but softens initial steering response.

parameters.label: Bump steer
parameters.what_it_does: Unwanted toe change as the front suspension compresses, set by steering-link height shims. Reducing bump steer keeps steering consistent over bumps and on entry; adding small amounts can tune mid-corner steering.

parameters.label: Front shock oil weight
parameters.what_it_does: Viscosity of damping fluid in the front shocks (cSt/wt). Thicker front oil slows front suspension movement, calming dive and initial steering and reducing bottoming; thinner oil reacts faster for more low-speed grip and bump compliance.

parameters.label: Rear shock oil weight
parameters.what_it_does: Viscosity of damping fluid in the rear shocks. Thicker rear oil slows rear movement, holding the chassis flatter on power and on landings; thinner oil increases rear compliance and forward bite over bumps.

parameters.label: Shock pistons (holes x bore)
parameters.what_it_does: Number and diameter of bleed holes in the shock piston, which set the damping curve independently of oil weight. Fewer/smaller holes = stiffer, more pack (high-speed damping); more/larger holes = freer, more low-speed compliance.

parameters.label: Front shock pistons
parameters.what_it_does: Front-specific piston hole count/diameter. Tunes the front damping curve and pack rate; pairs with front oil to set high- vs low-speed damping balance at the front.

parameters.label: Rear shock pistons
parameters.what_it_does: Rear-specific piston hole count/diameter. Tunes rear damping curve and pack; more holes free the rear for bumps, fewer add pack and hold-up on power and landings.

parameters.label: Front shock limiter (internal travel limiter)
parameters.what_it_does: Internal spacer that shortens up-travel on the shock shaft. More front limiter reduces front compression travel, raising effective front spring rate near full bump and limiting dive on landings.

parameters.label: Rear shock limiter
parameters.what_it_does: Internal up-travel limiter on the rear shocks. More rear limiter reduces rear compression near full bump, controlling squat and bottoming on big landings.

parameters.label: Front shock position (tower / arm hole)
parameters.what_it_does: Which mounting hole the front shock uses on the tower and arm, changing leverage ratio and shock angle. More inboard/laid-down = softer, more progressive front; more upright/outboard = stiffer, more reactive front.

parameters.label: Rear shock position (tower / arm hole)
parameters.what_it_does: Mounting-hole choice for the rear shock on tower and arm. Adjusts rear leverage ratio/progression and roll stiffness — laid-down softens and adds bump grip, upright stiffens and steadies.

parameters.label: Front shock angle
parameters.what_it_does: Lean angle of the front shock set by tower hole. More laid-down (leaned) increases progression and softens early travel; more upright makes the front more reactive and supportive.

parameters.label: Rear shock angle
parameters.what_it_does: Lean angle of the rear shock. Laid-down rear adds roll and progression for bump grip; upright rear adds support and on-power hold-up.

parameters.label: Front shock length
parameters.what_it_does: Built length of the front shock (eyelet spacing/spacers), which sets available travel and works with ride height and droop. Longer adds travel for rough tracks.

parameters.label: Rear shock length
parameters.what_it_does: Built length of the rear shock. Sets rear travel envelope alongside ride height and limiters; longer for rough/big-jump tracks.

parameters.label: Shock build (bladder vs emulsion)
parameters.what_it_does: Whether shocks use a bladder (air separated from oil) or emulsion (air mixed in) to handle volume compensation. Bladder gives consistent, less progressive damping; emulsion is more progressive and simpler but more temperature-sensitive.

parameters.label: Front springs
parameters.what_it_does: Spring rate at the front, the primary control of front roll stiffness and ride support. Stiffer front springs reduce dive and steering and add stability; softer front springs add front grip and bump compliance.

parameters.label: Rear springs
parameters.what_it_does: Spring rate at the rear, the primary control of rear roll stiffness and squat. Stiffer rear springs add on-power stability and reduce squat; softer rear springs add forward bite and rough-track traction.

parameters.label: Spring preload / collar
parameters.what_it_does: Pre-compression of the spring via threaded collar or clips, used to set ride height without changing spring rate (and slightly affecting initial support). Mostly a ride-height adjuster.

parameters.label: Front differential oil
parameters.what_it_does: Viscosity of fluid in a gear-type front diff. Thicker front diff oil tightens the front diff, reducing corner-entry steering and adding mid-corner front traction and stability; thinner frees entry steering.

parameters.label: Center differential oil
parameters.what_it_does: Viscosity of fluid in the center diff splitting torque front/rear. Thicker center oil locks the drivetrain for forward drive and acceleration but reduces steering and adds push; thinner frees rotation and steering.

parameters.label: Rear differential oil
parameters.what_it_does: Viscosity of fluid in a gear-type rear diff. Thicker rear diff oil tightens the rear, smoothing on-power delivery and adding stability/forward bite; thinner frees rotation and adds off-power steering.

parameters.label: Differential type (gear vs ball vs spool vs one-way)
parameters.what_it_does: The differential mechanism itself: gear/fluid diff, ball diff, solid spool, or one-way. Determines whether and how the axle differentiates; a spool locks the axle for max drive, a one-way frees off-power for coast steering.

parameters.label: Ball-diff tension
parameters.what_it_does: How tightly a ball differential is set, controlling slip torque. Tighter ball diff drives harder out of corners and resists slip; looser allows more differentiation and is more forgiving on power.

parameters.label: Front one-way / spool option
parameters.what_it_does: Front drive device choice (one-way, spool, or diff). A front one-way frees the front off-throttle for sharp entry/coast steering but removes front engine-braking; a spool maximises front drive.

parameters.label: Front sway/anti-roll bar
parameters.what_it_does: Wire bar linking the front wheels that resists body roll at the front. A thicker/stiffer front bar reduces front roll for less steering and more stability; thinner/softer (or removed) adds front grip and roll.

parameters.label: Rear sway/anti-roll bar
parameters.what_it_does: Wire bar linking the rear wheels that resists rear body roll. A thicker/stiffer rear bar reduces rear roll for more steering and rotation but less rear traction; thinner/softer (or removed) adds rear grip and resists traction roll.

parameters.label: Sway-bar mount / on-off
parameters.what_it_does: Whether an anti-roll bar is fitted at all and how it mounts, since many entry/mid models ship without bar mounts. Adding a bar is a major roll-stiffness lever only available on equipped chassis.

parameters.label: Front ride height
parameters.what_it_does: Static chassis height at the front. Lower front lowers the front roll couple for more steering and high-speed stability but risks bottoming; higher front clears bumps and softens steering.

parameters.label: Rear ride height
parameters.what_it_does: Static chassis height at the rear. Lower rear adds rear stability and lowers CG; higher rear adds rear weight transfer and forward bite and helps clear rough sections.

parameters.label: Ride height (overall, engine alias)
parameters.what_it_does: Engine-canonical overall ride-height setting. Lower = lower CG, more stability and steering, less bump clearance; higher = more clearance and weight transfer, softer handling.

parameters.label: Ride-height rake (front-rear difference)
parameters.what_it_does: The front-to-rear ride-height difference. More rake (rear higher than front) shifts the balance toward more steering/rotation; less rake or nose-up reduces steering and adds rear stability.

parameters.label: Front droop / downstop
parameters.what_it_does: Amount of front down-travel (droop) before the suspension tops out. More front droop lets the front extend for more forward weight transfer and steering on entry; less front droop keeps the front flatter and more stable.

parameters.label: Rear droop / downstop
parameters.what_it_does: Amount of rear down-travel. More rear droop adds rear forward-bite and rough-track traction by letting the rear extend; less rear droop keeps the rear flatter for stability and jumping.

parameters.label: Rear downstop (engine alias of rear_droop)
parameters.what_it_does: Engine-canonical rear downstop/droop setting. More droop = more rear traction and weight transfer; less = flatter, more stable, better jumping.

parameters.label: Ballast / added weight
parameters.what_it_does: Lead/brass/tungsten weight added to the chassis to tune total mass and balance. Adding weight low and central can improve grip and stability on high-bite tracks; its position shifts front/rear and corner balance.

parameters.label: Weight / CG position (front-rear bias)
parameters.what_it_does: Where mass (battery, ballast, engine) sits along the chassis, setting static front/rear weight distribution. Rearward bias adds forward bite and reduces steering; forward bias adds steering and reduces rear traction.

parameters.label: Battery position
parameters.what_it_does: Mounting location of the battery pack (front/mid/rear, in-line/saddle). Moves a large mass to tune weight distribution, polar moment and corner weights — a primary balance lever on electric cars.

parameters.label: Pinion gear
parameters.what_it_does: Tooth count of the motor pinion. More pinion teeth raise top speed and lower acceleration/torque (and raise motor temperature); fewer add punch and run cooler.

parameters.label: Spur gear
parameters.what_it_does: Tooth count of the spur/crown gear meshing with the pinion. With pinion it sets primary gear ratio: more spur teeth = lower (more torque/cooler), fewer spur teeth = higher (faster/hotter).

parameters.label: Final drive ratio (FDR)
parameters.what_it_does: Overall reduction from motor to wheels (pinion/spur x internal x diff). Higher FDR = more torque and acceleration, lower top speed and cooler motor; lower FDR = more speed, more heat.

parameters.label: Internal / transmission ratio
parameters.what_it_does: Fixed reduction inside the transmission/diffs that multiplies into FDR. Usually set by kit but selectable on some chassis to shift the whole gearing window.

parameters.label: 2-speed shift point
parameters.what_it_does: On nitro on-road/large-scale 2-speed gearboxes, the RPM at which it shifts from 1st to 2nd. Later shift keeps the car in 1st longer for acceleration; earlier shift favours top-end and smoothness.

parameters.label: Clutch (springs/shoes/bell)
parameters.what_it_does: Nitro clutch engagement, set by spring rate, shoe material/count and clutch-bell teeth. Tunes how aggressively power hits the drivetrain off the line and out of slow corners.

parameters.label: Slipper clutch
parameters.what_it_does: Friction clutch on the spur that slips under sharp load. Looser slipper cushions power for traction and protects the drivetrain on jumps; tighter delivers more direct drive and acceleration.

parameters.label: Front tyre compound
parameters.what_it_does: Rubber hardness of the front tyres. Softer compound adds front grip on low-bite/cold surfaces but wears and heats faster; harder compound suits high-bite/abrasive/hot tracks and lasts longer.

parameters.label: Rear tyre compound
parameters.what_it_does: Rubber hardness of the rear tyres. Softer adds rear traction on low grip but overheats on high bite; harder suits abrasive/high-bite/hot conditions and lasts longer.

parameters.label: Front tyre tread / profile
parameters.what_it_does: The tread pattern and carcass profile of the front tyre, matched to surface type (loose dirt, hard-pack, astroturf, carpet, asphalt). Drives mechanical grip and how the tyre keys into the surface.

parameters.label: Rear tyre tread / profile
parameters.what_it_does: Tread pattern and carcass profile of the rear tyre, matched to surface. Primary mechanical-grip selector for forward drive on the given surface.

parameters.label: Tyre insert / foam
parameters.what_it_does: Foam (or molded) insert inside the tyre setting its sidewall stiffness and shape under load. Firmer inserts add support and steering on high bite; softer inserts add grip and conform on rough/low-bite tracks.

parameters.label: Tyre additive / prep / traction compound
parameters.what_it_does: Chemical treatment applied to the tyre (traction additive, sauce) and soak time to soften the surface and add grip. A major grip lever on carpet/asphalt; class-legality and timing matter.

parameters.label: Tyre gluing / truing / diameter
parameters.what_it_does: How the tyre is glued to the wheel and trued to a diameter. Outer diameter changes effective gearing and ride height; trued/balanced tyres run truer at speed.

parameters.label: Motor wind (turns / KV)
parameters.what_it_does: The motor's winding spec (turns for brushless sensored, KV for many systems) setting its base RPM and torque. Lower turns / higher KV = more power and speed; higher turns / lower KV = milder, cooler, more controllable.

parameters.label: Motor timing
parameters.what_it_does: Mechanical/endbell timing advance on the motor. More timing adds power and RPM but raises heat and shortens motor life; less timing is cooler and more efficient.

parameters.label: ESC boost timing
parameters.what_it_does: RPM-dependent timing the ESC adds electronically (modified/blinky-off classes). More boost increases top-end power and RPM with more heat; tunes the power curve without changing the motor.

parameters.label: ESC turbo timing
parameters.what_it_does: Extra timing the ESC slams in at full throttle/top RPM. More turbo adds straightaway top speed at the cost of heat and battery; the turbo activation/ramp tunes how abruptly it hits.

parameters.label: Throttle curve / EPA
parameters.what_it_does: Transmitter/ESC mapping of trigger travel to throttle output. A softer/exponential curve smooths low-bite throttle response and helps traction; a linear/aggressive curve gives more direct response.

parameters.label: Brake curve / strength
parameters.what_it_does: Mapping and maximum strength of the brakes. Softer initial brake aids stability into corners on low grip; stronger brakes shorten braking but can lock and unsettle entry.

parameters.label: Drag brake
parameters.what_it_does: Automatic braking the ESC applies at neutral throttle. More drag brake slows the car when you release the trigger for tighter corner entry and engine-brake feel; less lets it coast.

parameters.label: Brake bias (front/rear)
parameters.what_it_does: On dual-brake (mostly nitro) cars, how braking force splits front/rear. More front bias shortens stops and adds entry steering but risks nose-dive/locking; more rear bias stabilises but lengthens braking.

parameters.label: Steering curve / dual-rate / EPA
parameters.what_it_does: Transmitter mapping of steering input to servo travel (rate, exponential, endpoints). Reduces twitchiness at center and tunes how aggressive steering feels; an aid layered on mechanical steering.

parameters.label: Gyro gain (steering stability)
parameters.what_it_does: How strongly an electronic gyro counter-steers to stabilise the car. More gain adds high-speed/low-grip stability and catches slides; too much makes the car feel laggy or fight the driver.

parameters.label: Wing angle
parameters.what_it_does: Angle of attack of the rear wing. More wing angle adds rear downforce for high-speed stability and rear grip but adds drag and slows top speed; less frees speed and rotation.

parameters.label: Wing position / mounting
parameters.what_it_does: Fore/aft and height mounting of the rear wing. Moving the wing back/up increases its effect and rear stability; the gurney/wickerbill choice further tunes downforce.

parameters.label: Body shell choice
parameters.what_it_does: Which body shell is fitted, setting aero balance, downforce and drag. A higher-downforce body adds stability/steering at speed; a low-drag body favours top speed.

parameters.label: Body / cab-forward position & mounting height
parameters.what_it_does: Fore/aft and height mounting of the body. Moving the body forward shifts aero balance forward for more front bite; height affects downforce and how air loads each axle.

parameters.label: Front splitter / wickerbill / gurney
parameters.what_it_does: Aero add-ons at the front (splitter, gurney lip) or on the wing that increase local downforce. Adds front grip or wing effect in small, tunable increments.

parameters.label: Chassis stiffener / brace
parameters.what_it_does: Optional braces, top decks or stiffening plates that change how much the chassis twists. More stiffness adds responsiveness and consistency on high bite; more flex adds mechanical grip and forgiveness on low bite.

parameters.label: Shock tower / tower thickness
parameters.what_it_does: Thickness/material of the shock towers, which flex under load. Thicker/stiffer towers sharpen response; thinner towers add compliance and grip on rough/low-bite tracks.

parameters.label: Chassis / suspension slop control
parameters.what_it_does: Eliminating or tuning play in hinge pins, bushings and links via shims. Less slop makes the car consistent and precise; deliberate slop can free up binding suspension.

symptoms.label: Corner-entry understeer (push on entry)
pilot_phrases: won't bite when I let off

symptoms.label: On-power push
pilot_phrases: pushes when I get on the gas

symptoms.label: Power-on oversteer (loose on throttle)
pilot_phrases: rear breaks loose on the gas

symptoms.label: Off-throttle / corner-entry instability
pilot_phrases: rear gets light when I lift

symptoms.label: Lazy / numb / slow steering
pilot_phrases: have to wait for it to turn

symptoms.label: Lack of forward bite (poor drive out)
pilot_phrases: won't hook up out of corners

symptoms.label: Low overall grip / car slides everywhere
Jump balance (noses down / kicks up)
pilot_phrases: kicks the rear up on jumps

option_classes.label: Adjustable / removable anti-roll bars
option_classes.typical_presence: Kit-standard front+rear on high-end 1/8 and 1/10 race buggies; often a single bar, optional, or absent on entry/mid 2WD and many RTR/sport chassis.
example_models_without: some entry 1/10 buggies (front bar only or none)
option_classes.notes: A sway bar is the single biggest roll-stiffness lever; if the model has no bar mount, every sway-bar rule must refuse and fall back to springs/shock-position.

option_classes.label: Sway-bar mount / hardware kit
option_classes.typical_presence: Sold as an option part to add a bar to chassis whose arms/bulkheads are pre-drilled but ship without the bar hardware.
example_models_with: mid-tier buggies with optional rear-bar kits
example_models_without: chassis with no bar provision at all
option_classes.notes: Distinct from the bars themselves: the mounting points must exist or be addable before any bar advice applies.

option_classes.label: Gear-diff (fluid diff) conversion
option_classes.typical_presence: Standard fluid diffs on 1/8 and most 1/10 4WD; on 1/10 2WD and some 4WD a ball diff is standard and a gear-diff is an optional conversion (or vice versa).
option_classes.notes: All diff-oil rules require a fluid diff at that position; on a ball-diff car they must remap to ball_diff_tension or refuse.

option_classes.label: Adjustable shock towers / multiple shock positions
option_classes.typical_presence: Multiple tower+arm holes are kit-standard on race chassis; entry models often have a single fixed position.
option_classes.notes: Shock-position/angle advice must be gated on whether alternative holes exist on that exact tower/arm.

option_classes.label: Anti-squat / anti-dive / kick-up inserts
option_classes.typical_presence: Interchangeable inserts/bushings are kit-standard on high-end offroad; fixed geometry on many sport/entry chassis.
option_classes.notes: Anti-squat/anti-dive are offroad-only and insert-gated; refuse on cars with fixed suspension blocks.

option_classes.label: Adjustable Ackermann
option_classes.typical_presence: Multiple Ackermann plate/post positions are common on race touring and high-end buggies; fixed on entry models.
option_classes.notes: Only advise Ackermann when the steering rack/plate offers alternative holes.

option_classes.label: Adjustable wheelbase
option_classes.typical_presence: Set by rear-hub or arm shims on most race chassis; fixed on many sport/RTR models.
option_classes.notes: Wheelbase advice requires shim provision at the hubs/arms.

option_classes.label: Brass / tungsten weight (ballast) kit
option_classes.typical_presence: Brass/tungsten chassis weights, motor mounts and bulkheads are optional tuning parts; not present on stock cars.
example_models_with: modern 1/10 race chassis with brass option ranges (AE, XRAY, TLR)
example_models_without: stock-weight cars before option parts are added
option_classes.notes: Weight-position advice is only actionable if the driver has weights and mount points; otherwise it is a buy-this-part suggestion, not a free setup change.

option_classes.label: Ride-height clips vs threaded collars
option_classes.typical_presence: Threaded shock collars (fine, continuous) on race shocks; preload clips/spacers (coarse, stepped) on entry shocks.
option_classes.notes: Ride height is universally adjustable, but resolution differs — clip cars can only move in discrete spacer steps, so magnitude_guidance must respect that.

option_classes.label: Bladder vs emulsion shock build
option_classes.typical_presence: Bladder shocks standard on most 1/8 and many 1/10 race kits; emulsion common on some 1/10 and sport shocks.
option_classes.notes: Build type changes how oil-weight advice translates (emulsion is more progressive and temperature-sensitive); note it but rarely the primary lever.

option_classes.label: Adjustable bellcrank / servo-saver
option_classes.typical_presence: Adjustable-tension servo-savers and multi-hole bellcranks on race chassis; fixed plastic savers on entry cars.
example_models_with: most current race touring and buggy chassis
option_classes.notes: Affects steering geometry and feel; gate Ackermann/bump-steer tweaks on bellcrank adjustability.

option_classes.label: Adjustable roll-center / camber links
option_classes.typical_presence: Multiple inner/outer ball-stud and shim positions on race chassis; fixed turnbuckle mounts on entry models.
example_models_with: XRAY/AE/TLR race kits with ball-stud shim ranges
option_classes.notes: Roll-center advice requires alternative link positions/shims; on fixed cars only camber (turnbuckle length) is adjustable.

option_classes.label: Internal shock travel limiters
option_classes.typical_presence: Internal limiter spacers are standard tuning parts on 1/8 and 1/10 4WD race shocks; absent on simpler shocks.
option_classes.notes: Limiter advice needs shocks that accept internal spacers; otherwise remap to droop/down-travel limiting.

option_classes.label: Electronic gyro / stability unit
option_classes.typical_presence: Common/expected on 1/8 nitro on-road, GT, rally and drift; optional add-on elsewhere and banned in some classes.
example_models_without: most stock offroad club classes (often rules-banned)
option_classes.notes: Gyro advice is only valid if a gyro is fitted and class-legal; otherwise refuse.

option_classes.label: 2-speed gearbox
option_classes.typical_presence: Standard on 1/8 nitro on-road and large-scale; absent on offroad and electric.
option_classes.notes: Shift-point advice only applies to 2-speed-equipped nitro on-road/large-scale.

option_classes.label: ESC boost/turbo capability (class-gated)
option_classes.typical_presence: Modified/open ESCs allow boost+turbo; spec/blinky classes lock timing at zero by rule.
option_classes.notes: Boost/turbo advice must be gated on class legality, not just hardware — refuse in blinky spec classes.

option_classes.label: Front one-way / spool / diff option
option_classes.typical_presence: Selectable front drive device on 1/10 4WD, touring and pan; fixed on most offroad.
option_classes.notes: Coast-steering advice via a front one-way only applies where that device is fitted.
